analysis.title: Impartial analysis of Measure W

text: IMPARTIAL ANALYSIS OF MEASURE [TBD]
The California Constitution and Education Code authorize a school district to issue bonds for specified purposes if approved at an election by 55% of those voting on issuance of the bonds.

The Board of Trustees of the San Mateo-Foster City School District (District) proposes this Measure, which would authorize the District to issue bonds in a principal amount not to exceed $498 million. The bonds will have an interest rate not exceeding the legal maximum and will be repaid within the time permitted by law. The Tax Rate Statement printed in this pamphlet contains the District's best estimates of tax rates required to service the bond debt during the life of the bonds, which is anticipated to last until fiscal year 2054-55. The District's best estimate of the average annual tax rate levy to fund this bond is $29.00 per $100,000 ($0.029/$100) of assessed valuation. The District estimates that the total amount repayable during the life of the bond, including principal and interest, will be approximately $900 million.

The California Constitution requires the listing of specific projects to be funded from the bond revenue and certification that the District Board of Trustees has evaluated health, safety, class size reduction, classroom, educational, and information technology needs in the development of that list. The Bond Project List can be found in the full text of the Measure, and includes without limitation:

Restore shop classes with-tools and equipment for modern skilled trades; Update classrooms and labs for science, technology, engineering, and math; Replace leaky roofs and old windows; Update aging fire alarms and add emergency communication systems; Provide affordable housing to attract and retain quality teachers and staff; Improve accessibility for students and staff with disabilities; Improve school safety and security; and Acquire, construct, and repair facilities, equipment, and sites.

The Measure authorizes equipment acquisition, upgrades, repairs, services, construction, and other items related to the listed projects. The Bond Project List does not imply a specific prioritization among the projects, and should be reviewed for further details.

No proceeds from the bonds shall be used for teacher or administrator salaries or other school operating expenses, except to reimburse the District for the cost of staff time spent working on the bond projects themselves.

State law requires that the District take certain steps to account for the proceeds from the bonds. Accordingly, the District will appoint an independent citizens' oversight committee, establish a special account for deposit of the bond proceeds, and conduct annual independent performance and financial audits to ensure that bond funds are spent only for the purposes listed in the Bond Project List and for no other purposes.
A "yes" vote on this Measure would authorize the District to issue bonds in a principal amount not to exceed $498 million for the purposes listed in the Bond Project List.
A "no" vote would prevent the District from issuing the bonds. [Ill This Measure passes if at least 55% of those voting on the Measure vote "yes."
---- End of Analysis -- (500 word limit. 471 words)

text: Argument in Favor of Measure Vote YES on Measure for our neighborhood schools in San Mateo and Foster City! Our San Mateo and Foster City neighborhood schools have served generations of local families. It's important to protect our strong neighborhood schools that prepare local kids with the skills they need to compete for college and jobs in a rapidly-changing economy. Great schools protect property values and benefit everyone — whether or not we have children or grandchildren in school. Our schools need: • Great teachers • Asafe environment for students and teachers • Strong programs in science, math, literacy, engineering and career technical education Classrooms that build vocational, hands-on and problem-solving skills for today's and tomorrow's careers Measure will meet all these goals, providing necessary school updates now and for generations to come. Yes on to repair 60-year-old school facilities, including aging underground pipes that risk sewer backups and expensive failures, leaky roofs, old plumbing, restrooms, windows and doors. Hazardous materials like lead and asbestos must be removed where they're still found. Yes on to upgrade wiring and tech infrastructure for up-to-date science, technology, engineering, and math instruction. Yes on to restore shop classes and expand career technical education/ vocational programs. Yes on to help our schools recruit and retain great teachers, who struggle with the high cost of living in our area, by repurposing old administrative buildings for teacher and staff housing. Yes on for essential security and fire safety upgrades, including fire alarms and emergency communication systems. Vote Yes on to ensure local control and oversight over school improvement funds: • Independent oversight, annual audits, and public spending disclosures

text: San Mateo-Foster City School District $498M Bond Measure

The San Mateo-Foster City School District is asking you to incur bond debt of $498 million. That's a debt you owe for the next 30 plus years. Have they earned it? The stats: • Loss of ADA enrollment from 2020-21 school year = 649 students • Percentage of students behind grade level in English = 47.26% • Percentage of students behind grade level in math = 50.57% Chronic absenteeism data = 16.2% • Teachers' salaries of $82,574 (2020-21) rose to $104,943 (2024-25) o An Increase = $22,369 Teacher's get pay raises while students test scores decline! Education Data Partnership (ED-DATA.ORG) shows enrollment of 9, 708 students. That's bond debt exceeding $51 ,297 per student -- NOT counting interest expense which usually doubles the cost. Does that do anything to help students? Clearly no. When you buy a home} truth in lending taws require that you be told the real total cost of buying that home. For example: • Borrowing $498,000,000; paying 3% interest for 30 years would incur interest expenses of approximately plus principal $498,000,000 for a lifetime total cost of of YOUR money! Consumer protection laws should apply to bond issues. As taxpayers, we deserve to know the full truth about Measure M. We don't even know when this debt will begin, let alone what the market interest rate will be, when it does. Just say no to bond debt. Question: will this bond measure fix declining English proficiency? NO! Question: will this bond measure fix declining math proficiency? NO! Question: will this bond measure fix declining enrollment? NO! Question: will this bond measure fix chronic absenteeism data? NO! Stop rewarding bad behavior. Vote NO tax increase! For more information, www.SVTaxpayers.org

text: REBUTTAL TO ARGUMENT IN FAVOR OF MEASURE W FACT: The real number is $900 million, not $498 million. • The District's own Tax Rate Statement discloses total principal and interest at approximately $900 million nearfy double what proponents advertise — collected through fiscal year 2054-55, nearly 30 years from now. FACT: This is the third major bond in about a decade. • Measure X ($148 million, 2015) and Measure T ($409 million, 2020) already funded roofs, wiring, fire alarms, and safety upgrades. Ask the District what those bonds fixed before handing over $498 million more for the same categories of need. FACT: The "project list" is a blank check. • The resolution itself states project budgets are estimates that "may be delayed or may not be completed," and lets the Board substitute demolition for repair at its own discretion. Independent oversight can confirm money was spent on the list — not that your priorities were funded. FACT: Teacher housing, with no separate budget disclosed. Bundled into this facilities bond is authority to "construct, acquire, or contribute to employee housing units" — with no dollar figure broken out for that use alone. FACT: The District's own polling found support barely above the threshold. • A 2025 District-commissioned survey found only —570/0 support for this exact bond amount — just above the 55% required to pass — yet the Board proceeded unchanged. Other polling - cost of living is too high, taxes are out of control, and funds are so mismanaged we can't trust the system. Vote NO on Measure W
SAN MATEO COUNTY

text: Rebuttal to the Argument Against Measure W L We appreciate the generic argument filed by our opponent. This is the same argument this group files against all school measures. in our area — regardless of the specific challenges facing our schools.

While they're entitled to their opinion, we know that student achievement is rising, not falling. Don't take our word for it. We encourage every voter to visit Niche.com, look up the San Mateo-Foster City School District, and see that our schools earn an "A" rating.
We also know that our neighborhood schools need urgent repairs to protect quality education at a time when State education funding is shrinking and Federal support is disappearing.
Vote YES on W to keep great teachers in our community at a time when the high cost of living is driving teachers away from the Peninsula.
Vote YES on W to restore vocational programs and shop classes to give our students practical, hands-on skills for future careers.

Vote YES on W to ensure every student in San Mateo and Foster City has access to a safe classroom that meets modern standards for fire and earthquake safety and access for disabled students — without any remaining lead or asbestos.
Vote YES on W to protect strong programs in science, math, literacy, engineering, technology, and career technical education.
Now is the time to protect OUR local schools. Vote YES on W to secure reliable, local funding for essential, urgent improvements that our teachers and students are counting on.
Vote YES on W for great teachers and safe schools!
SAN MATEO
